1. Heard Mr. Dev D Patel, learned advocate for the appellant.
Mr. Rashesh A Patel, learned advocate has entered his appearance on behalf of respondent nos. 1 to 5 - original claimants.

2. The present appeal is filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 at the instance of the original opponent no.1, who is driver cum owner of the offending vehicle being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 30.10.2021 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxi), Vadodara in MACP No.136 of 2011.

By the said impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has held the original opponent no.1 negligent and liable to pay an amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.2,00,500/- with interest at the rate of 9% p.a. from the date of filing of the claim petition till its actual realization with proportionate costs.

The Tribunal has further clarified that any amount of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/202/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/09/2025 undefined compensation awarded under Section 140 of the Motor Vehicle Act, being realized, the same shall be deducted from the aforesaid amount.

sentences.text: Learned advocate for the appellant at the outset has submitted that the Tribunal committed grave error in holding the present appellant solely negligent towards the occurrence of the accident.
3.1. The attention of this Court was invited to the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal while examining the issue of negligency.
It is averred in the claim petition that on the date of accident the deceased who was aged 67 years, was going on his two wheeler vehicle Luna to reach medical shop of ONGC.

When he was passing on road near ONGC gate, at that time, the appellant who was driving his scooter bearing registration no. GJ-6-AF-1194, collided with the back side of Luna which resulted in fall of the deceased causing accidental injuries on head, left hand palms,
below knee of both the legs as well as other parts of his body.
The deceased was admitted in the sterling hospital and expired on 04.02.2008.
3.2. Learned advocate has invited my attention to the aforesaid case pleaded by the claimants in light of the contents of the FIR, Panchnama and the charge-sheet produced on record.
It was submitted that it is so unfortunate incident where the appellant had lost his control over the vehicle because of his old age.
It was explained that due to sudden horn honked by the vehicle following his vehicle, he NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/202/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/09/2025 undefined lost control.
In the process, his vehicle had hit the vehicle of the deceased which has resulted into fall of the deceased from the scooter.

He has further submitted that the appellant was driving his vehicle with moderate speed as there is no evidence on record to establish that the deceased was driving at high speed and in rash and negligent manner, the Tribunal ought to have exonerated the appellant towards such liability to pay compensation.
Learned advocate therefore, submitted that the Tribunal committed error in holding that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the appellant.

3.3. On the issue of quantum of compensation, learned advocate has submitted that in absence of any proof of income, though the Tribunal has determined the income of the deceased as Rs.2900/-
per month, the same is based on the assumption and presumption.
It is an undisputed fact that the deceased was a retired employee with no source of income.
Even otherwise, the Tribunal ought not to have considered minimum wages in the facts of the case when it is an admitted position that the deceased was a retired government employee.

3.4. On the issue of deduction of 1/4th being considered towards personal and living expenses of the deceased while considering loss of dependency, learned advocate has submitted that indisputably the claimants includes wife of the deceased and their four major children which includes three married daughter of the deceased.

According to him, the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/202/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/09/2025 undefined Tribunal committed error in considering major childrens as dependent on the income of the deceased by erroneously applying 1/4th deduction instead of 1/3rd.

The reliance was placed on the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121.
3.5.

sentences.text: 5. Per contra, learned advocate Mr. Rashesh Patel appearing for the respondents- original claimants has vehemently objected to the aforesaid submissions.

Disputing the submissions made by the learned advocate for the appellant on the issue of negligency, learned advocate has pointed out that the Tribunal upon appreciation of the cogent material in the nature of FIR, panchnama of charge sheet produced on record has rightly arrived at a conclusion that accident had taken place because of the negligency of the appellant - original opponent.
He has further pointed out that the involvement of the vehicle is not disputed.

The occurrence of the accident is not disputed and therefore, merely because it is contended that the appellant was not driving vehicle in rash and negligent manner, the same cannot be considered as sole criteria while considering the issue of negligency.
He has therefore, urged this Court to not to entertain the present appeal.

On the issue of quantum of compensation, learned advocate has relied upon the findings and reasons recorded by the Tribunal and has submitted that the Tribunal has awarded just and proper compensation in the facts of the case which does not call for any interference.

Learned advocate has urged this Court to consider the object of the Motor Vehicles Act which aims at awarding just and proper amount of compensation, in absence of an appeal or any cross objection being filed, this Court being the Appellate Court can always modified the judgment in view of Order 41 Rule 33 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
He has therefore, urged this Court to invoke provisions of Order 41 Rule 33 of the Code in absence of any appeal or cross objection being filed.

5.2. As regards awarding interest on higher side is concerned, he submitted that as rightly pointed out in view of Section 171 of the Act of 1988, the discretion vested with the Tribunal to consider appropriate rate of interest and entitlement of such interest from such date.

The Tribunal in the facts of the case has judiciously applied its mind and has awarded interest at the rate of 9% from the date of filing of claim petition till its actual realization, which may not be interfered in absence of Ramsingh Sinhasansingh Nemdhari vs Sarojben Rammurti Sharma on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163938362/

6. Considering the aforesaid submissions of the learned advocates for the respective parties and having examined findings and the reasons assigned by the Tribunal in light of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/202/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/09/2025 undefined the evidence produced on record,
the only question which falls for consideration of this Court in the present appeal is as to whether the Tribunal committed any error in allowing the claim petition holding the present appellant solely negligent and liable to pay amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.2,00,500/-, in the facts of the case and the evidence brought on record, with interest at the rate of 9% with proportionate costs ?

7. I have carefully considered the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal on the issue of neligency, which is mainly based on the FIR produced on record at Exh.19, panchnama of the place of incident at Exh.20 and the copy of the charge sheet counter at Exh.24.

It is established through evidence of claimants that opponent -appellant herein has been charge-sheeted for the offence punishable under Sections 279, 337, 338 and 304(A) of the Indian Penal Code as well as Section 177 and 184 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
On the other hand, the opponent - appellant herein has chosen not to depose before the Tribunal and lead any evidence to substantiate his defence.

In such circumstances, the Tribunal has followed the principles laid down in the case of Vidhyadhar vs.
Manek Rao reported in AIR 1999 SC 1441 and has drawn adverse inference against opponent- appellant herein, holding him solely negligent towards occurrence of accident.

sentences.text: On re-appreciation of the aforesaid documents in light of the case pleaded before the Tribunal as well as evidence of the claimant, it has clearly transpired on record that accident had occurred when the vehicle driven by NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/202/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/09/2025 undefined the present appellant had hit from backside of the vehicle going ahead which was driven by the deceased.

Because of the collision with the vehicle of the deceased, it had resulted into fall of the deceased,
resultantly the deceased had sustained serious head injuries.

The medical case papers of the deceased has been produced on record along with list of documents, the postmortem report is produced on record at Exh.22 wherein cause of death is reported due to shock and hemorrhage following head injuries.

Considering the aforesaid documents on record, in the opinion of this Court,
no error can be found with the aforesaid findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal leading to the conclusion that the accident had taken place because of the negligency of the present appellant.

8. On the issue of quantum of compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has also noted that the deceased has retired from ONGC whereby he was receiving pension of amount of Rs.5,000/-.However, the Tribunal has in absence of proof of documents relating to pension of Rs.5,000/- and additional income of Rs.3,000/- as claimed of being earned by deceased by doing job of store keeper in private firm, has followed the standard rates of minimum wages prescribed by the State Government.
The Tribunal has noted that the accident has taken place in the month of December 2008 and the minimum wages prevailing on the aforesaid date was Rs.2900/-.
Thus, the Tribunal has determined the notional income of the deceased as Rs.2900/- per month.
Noticing the age of the deceased as 67 years, the Tribunal has rightly not considered NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/202/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/09/2025 undefined the future prospect.

In my view, in absence of proof of income being brought on record, the Tribunal has rightly applied minimum Ramsingh Sinhasansingh Nemdhari vs Sarojben Rammurti Sharma on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163938362/

sentences.text: 8.1. The Tribunal has thereafter considered the number of dependents of the deceased and has deducted 1/4th towards personal and living expenses.
Admittedly, the deceased was survived by widow and four major children which includes three married daughters.
From the record, it is evident that the major son of the deceased was occupied in service and was therefore, as such is financially not dependent on the income of the deceased.
In this regard, it would be appropriate to consider the legal position as laid down in the case of Jitender Kumar and Anr vs. Sanjay Prasad and others rendered in Civil Appeal No.7199 of 2025.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court while dealing with issue of dependency in case of deceased aged 64 years, entertaining the appeal preferred by the claimants, who were married and financially independent, held that the legal representative's entitlement to compensation is not contingent upon financial dependency.

Applying the principles laid down in its earlier decision in case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Birendra reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356 and in case of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/202/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/09/2025 undefined Seema Rani and ors vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited reported in (2025) SCC Online SC 283, the Court reiterated that even married and financially independent children are eligible to claim compensation as legal heirs.

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid principles in the facts of the case, though the childrens of the deceased were not dependent financially on the income of the deceased, however, claim petition at their instance is maintainable and they are also held entitled to receive compensation as his legal representatives.

8.2. Having held so, as regards deduction to be applied towards personal expenses of deceased is concerned, considering the principles of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma (supra) as well as Jitender Kumar (supra) the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should have been considered  instead of 1/4th.

Considering the submissions made by the learned advocates for the respective parties on the issue of Order 41 Rule 33 of the Code and the rate of interest and its entitlement is concerned, looking to the benevolent scheme of the Act, which puts the obligation on the Court / Tribunal to determine just and proper amount of compensation, in the facts of the case considering the claimants which includes widow of the deceased, three major daughters and elder son, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra) and in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd (supra), whereby their right to seek compensation towards parental and filial consortium, each of the claimants shall be entitled to amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.44,000/- each.
Thus, the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is required to be modified inasmuch as amount of loss of consortium is determined as Rs.2.20 lakhs.
As regards the amount of compensation under the head of funeral expenses and loss of estate is concerned, the same is also required to be reconsidered as Rs.18,150/- each.

Thus, total amount of compensation awarded under the conventional heads is reconsidered as Rs.2,56,300/-.
10.
This brings me to the issue of rate of interest being determined by the Tribunal as 9% on higher side on the total amount of compensation by the Tribunal.

I have given my thoughtful consideration to the various judgments relied upon NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/202/2022 JUDGMENT DATED:
08/09/2025 undefined by the learned advocate for the appellant in this regard.

The rate of interest as rightly pointed out by the learned advocate for the appellant is governed by Section 171 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 wherein the discretion is vested with the Tribunal to award simple rate of interest at such rate and from such date as the Tribunal may consider in the facts of the case,
however the only curtailment it places is same may not be earlier than the date of making of claim.
Considering the aforesaid provision in the facts of the case on hand, it is evident from the record that the accident had taken place way back in the year 2008.
The claim petition which was preferred in 2011 came to be decided and disposed of by impugned judgment and award passed in the year 2021.
All throughout these years, the original claimants have patiently waited for adjudication of their right to seek compensation under the Motor Vehicles Act.

Considering the aforesaid circumstances on record and the time consumed in concluding the proceedings, the Tribunal has rightly awarded interest at the rate of 9% on the total amount of compensation from the date of filing of the claim petition till its actual realization.

sentences.text: For the foregoing reasons, though the appeal is partly allowed on the issue of deduction applied in computing loss of dependency, however qua other issues the same is not entertained.

Thus, the impugned judgment and award dated 30.10.2021 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxi), Vadodara in MACP No.136 of 2011 is hereby modified by holding the respondents - original claimants entitled to additional amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.1,42,800/-.
Let, the aforesaid additional amount of compensation be deposited with the concerned Tribunal within a period of 8 weeks from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this order.

In case,
if the appellant fails to deposit the aforesaid amount of compensation within stipulated period, the respondents - original claimants shall be entitled to 6% simple interest on such additional amount of compensation from the date of order pronounced till its actual realization.
With these observations, present First Appeal stands disposed of.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
M/s. Shriram Genearl Insurance Company vs. Surekha reported in 2020 ACJ 434.
It is established through evidence of claimants that opponent -appellant herein has been charge-sheeted for the offence punishable under Sections 279, 337, 338 and 304(A) of the Indian Penal Code as well as Section 177 and 184 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
In such circumstances, the Tribunal has followed the principles laid down in the case of Vidhyadhar vs.
Manek Rao reported in AIR 1999 SC 1441 and has drawn adverse inference against opponent- appellant herein, holding him solely negligent towards occurrence of accident.
On re-appreciation of the aforesaid documents in light of the case pleaded before the Tribunal as well as evidence of the claimant, it has clearly transpired on record that accident had occurred when the vehicle driven by NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/202/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/09/2025 undefined the present appellant had hit from backside of the vehicle going ahead which was driven by the deceased.
Because of the collision with the vehicle of the deceased, it had resulted into fall of the deceased,
resultantly the deceased had sustained serious head injuries.
The medical case papers of the deceased has been produced on record along with list of documents, the postmortem report is produced on record at Exh.22 wherein cause of death is reported due to shock and hemorrhage following head injuries.
Considering the aforesaid documents on record, in the opinion of this Court,
no error can be found with the aforesaid findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal leading to the conclusion that the accident had taken place because of the negligency of the present appellant.
From the record, it is evident that the major son of the deceased was occupied in service and was therefore, as such is financially not dependent on the income of the deceased.
Hence, applying the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of New India Assurance Co. Limited vs. Sonigra Juhi Uttamchand reported in neutral citation 2025 INSC 15, more so para 9, the claimant shall be entitled to enhancement of amount of compensation NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/202/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/09/2025 undefined under the conventional heads.
The rate of interest as rightly pointed out by the learned advocate for the appellant is governed by Section 171 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 wherein the discretion is vested with the Tribunal to award simple rate of interest at such rate and from such date as the Tribunal may consider in the facts of the case,
however the only curtailment it places is same may not be earlier than the date of making of claim.
Considering the aforesaid circumstances on record and the time consumed in concluding the proceedings, the Tribunal has rightly awarded interest at the rate of 9% on the total amount of compensation from the date of filing of the claim petition till its actual realization.
